//J U D G M E N T//

This claim petition is filed by the petitioners claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the death of Sri.Srinivasa S/o. Late Channaiah in a Road Traffic Accident.

2. The petition averments in brief is that:-
 That the petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 and 3 are the daughters of deceased Srinivasa S/o.Late Channaiah.

That on 19.03.2020 at about 8.15 p.m., the deceased was pedestrian near Vinayaka Nagara,
 SCCH-9 3 MVC.No.1763/2020 Ramanagara, at that time the driver of Ape Auto bearing Reg.No.KA-11-B-3855 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the deceased.
Due to impact, deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Thereafter he was shifted to Govt.
Hospital, Ramanagara.
In spite of the treatment given he could not survive.
Thereafter the Post Mortem was conducted and dead body was handed over to the petitioners.

The petitioners have spent Rs.2,00,000/-
Vasanthi vs Channakeshava on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92912475/
2 towards medical expenses, transportation of dead body,
funeral and other obsequies ceremonies.
Prior to the accident, deceased was hale and healthy and was working as mason and earning Rs.18,000/- p.m.
The petitioners have lost all his income, the deceased was the only bread earner of their family and all the family members were depending upon deceased for their livelihood.
The accident in question was occurred due to rash and negligent driver of the offending vehicle.
In this regard, a case has been registered in Ramanagara Town Circle Police Station in Cr.No.40/2020 for the offence  SCCH-9 4 MVC.No.1763/2020 punishable U/sec 279 & 304A of IPC.

The respondent No.1 and 2 being owner and insurer of offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners, who are wife and daughters of deceased and lost their bread earner in the accident.
Hence, petitioners constrained to file a petition for compensation.
3. After service of notice the respondent No.1 though appeared through his advocate but not filed written statement.
The respondent No.2 appeared through its advocate and filed its written statement.

The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 are as under:
 This respondent has admitted the issuance of policy Vasanthi vs Channakeshava on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92912475/
3 in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of APE Auto bearing Reg.No.KA-11-B-3855 and the liability is subject to policy conditions, valid and effective driving license held by the driver of Auto, valid Permit RC, FC and also subject to confirmation of 64 VB of Insurance Act.
As per Sec 134(c) of MV Act.
It is mandatory duty to submit all the vehicular  SCCH-9 5 MVC.No.1763/2020 documents to the concerned Police.
It has contended that the Ape Auto rickshaw was falsely implicated by the petitioners colluding with the owner of the vehicle and the Police to get compensation.
The driver of the alleged auto was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident and the vehicle was not having valid permit to ply in place of accident.

It has also denied the age,
occupation and income of the deceased and also relationship of the petitioners with that of the deceased.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, it has prayed to dismiss the petition.
4. On the basis of above pleadings my learned predecessor in office has framed the following issues.
ISSUES  1. Whether petitioners prove that, they are  the legal heirs of the deceased Sri.Srinivasa?

2. Whether petitioners prove that,
 Srinivasa died on account of Road Traffic  Accident took place on BM Road, Allahabad  Bank, Vinayakanagara, Ramanagara Town, due  to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Vasanthi vs Channakeshava on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92912475/
4  SCCH-9 6 MVC.No.1763/2020  Ape Auto bearing Reg.No.KA 11-B-3855 on  19.03.2020 at about 8.15 p.m?
 3.
Whether the petitioners are entitled for  compensation as claimed?

If so, to what  amount and from whom?
 4. What order or award?
5. In order to prove the case the wife of deceased got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P10.
On the other hand, the Asst. Manager of Respondent No.2 was examined as RW1 and no documents were got marked and closed the side.
6. I have heard the arguments and perused the records.

The learned counsel for respondent has relied upon judgment in - MFA 7404/2014 (MV-D), (Smt.Mariyamma &
Others V/s Suyambulingam.V & anr.)
 7.

My answer to the above issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 & 2: In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.3: Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.4:

Issue No.1 & 2:- It is the specific case of the petitioners that on 19.03.2020 at about 8.15 p.m., the deceased Srinivasa met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of driver of Ape Auto and due to said Vasanthi vs Channakeshava on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92912475/
5 accident deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to death.

9. In order to prove the case, the petitioner No.1 has filed affidavit in lieu of chief examination and examined as PW1 and reiterated all the facts mentioned in her petition and got marked documents at Ex.P1 to P10.
I have perused these documents cautiously.

The Ex.P1 is the FIR, Ex.P2 is the complaint, Ex.P3 is the mahazar, Ex.P4 is the inquest report, Ex.P5 is the PM report, Ex.P6 is the charge sheet,
Ex.P7 & 8 are the Aadhaar cards of petitioners, Ex.P9 is the IMV Report and Ex.P10 is the Election Identity Card of 1 st petitioner.

10 . On perusal of these documents, it shows that one Raju S/o.Muniyappa had lodged first Information before Ramanagara Traffic Police Station, alleging that on  SCCH-9 8 MVC.No.1763/2020 19.03.2020, the deceased was met with an accident due to rash and negligent riding of driver of offending vehicle.
On the basis of this first Information the Ramanagara Traffic Police have registered the case in Cr.No.40/2020 for the offence punishable Under Sec.279 & 304(A) of IPC and Sec.187 of M.V.Act.

Thereafter, the Investigation Officer had conducted the Investigation and filed the Charge Sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle by name Suresh.H S/o.P.Honnaiah for the offence punishable Under Sec. 279 & 304(A) of IPC.

Vasanthi vs Channakeshava on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92912475/
6  11.
The respondent No.2 in order to rebut the case of the petitioners it has examined its Asst. Manager as RW1 but he was not tendered for cross-examination.
As stated above, it is the case of the petitioners that deceased was dead due to accident caused by driver of offending vehicle.
No doubt, the PW1 is not a eyewitness to the accident.

However, it is settled principles of law that the petitioners in claim petition must prove the case by independently. The PW1 was elaborately cross-examined by the counsel for  SCCH-9 9 MVC.No.1763/2020 respondent No.2 but nothing was elicited to disbelieve her evidence.
Apart from this, the hand sketch produced along with Ex.P3 clearly goes to show that the accident was occurred on extreme left side of the Bengaluru-Mysuru Road.
Even the aforesaid sketch also goes to show that the said road is a one way road having sufficient width.
Though road is having sufficient width, the driver of offending vehicle drove the vehicle extreme left side of the road dashed against the deceased and caused the accident.
Apart from this, the Police records are clearly goes to show that the driver of offending vehicle has caused the accident by rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
Though Asst. Manager of respondent No.2 examined as RW1 but he remained absent and not tendered for cross- examination.

Hence, the evidence of RW1 cannot be looked into as it is not admissible evidence and it can be Vasanthi vs Channakeshava on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92912475/
7 considered as no evidence at all.

sentences.text: 12. That apart in a claim petition arising out of the accident the proving of negligence of offending vehicle is  SCCH-9 10 MVC.No.1763/2020 only preponderance of probabilities and not standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt as required in criminal case.
This principles of law was laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karanataka, in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum & Others V/s Satbir & others).

Further, the document Ex.P7, P8 & P10 are the Aadhaar cards and voter IDs of petitioners are clearly goes to show that the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 & 3 are the daughters of deceased Srinivasa.

Though 2 nd respondent contended that petitioners have to prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased person, but there is no serious dispute about relationship of petitioners with that of the deceased.
Therefore, the documents relied by petitioners are substantiate they are the legal heirs of deceased Srinivasa.
13 . It is true that there is a three days delay in lodging the complaint and registering the FIR.
The learned counsel for the 2nd respondent tried to elicited in the cross- examination of PW1 that there is three days delay in lodging  SCCH-9 11 MVC.No.1763/2020 the complaint.

Since the deceased has sustained severe Vasanthi vs Channakeshava on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92912475/
8 injuries and as such we cannot expect to lodge the complaint by the injured soon after the accident.

Normally,
injured person will give preference to take treatment rather than compliance of legal requirements. Same has been done in this case.
Therefore, the question of delay losses it significance.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in a reported decision - (2011) 4 SCC 693 Ravi V/s Bhadrinarayana, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that - " It is well settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case.

Knowing the Indian Conditions as they are,
we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after the accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of the kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
In cases of delay the Courts  SCCH-9 12 MVC.No.1763/2020 are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so, the contents of FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If the court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons, then even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be Vasanthi vs Channakeshava on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92912475/
9 dismissed merely on that ground.
The purpose of lodging the FIR in such type of cases is primarily to intimate the Police to initiate investigation of Criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves the factum of accident, so that victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay is doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

14. Under such circumstances, in the instant case,
there are sufficient materials to hold that the driver of offending vehicle has caused the accident with rash and negligent manner and as a result deceased received injuries and succumbed to death.
Under such circumstances, it is held that the petitioners have proved the issue No.1 & 2  SCCH-9 13 MVC.No.1763/2020
With these observations and discussion, I answered Issue No.1 & 2 in the affirmative.
15. Issue No.3:

In view of answering issue No.1 &
2 in the affirmative, the petitioners are entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like age, avocation, income of deceased, conveyance charges, funeral and obsequies,
towards loss of love and affection, etc., let me discuss one by one;
 (A) Towards Loss of dependency (loss of future Vasanthi vs Channakeshava on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92912475/
10 earnings):
i) In the petition the age of the deceased by name Srinivasa is shown as 40 years.
The petitioners have not produced any documents to show the age of the deceased as on the date of accident.
Under such circumstances, the medical records have to be considered for the purpose of determining the age of the deceased.
The Ex.P5/Post Mortem report of deceased, discloses age of the deceased  SCCH-9 14 MVC.No.1763/2020 as 40 years as on the date of accident.
Therefore, the age mentioned in the Ex.P5 is to be considered for calculation of the multiplier.
As per dictum of Hon'ble Supreme court of India in Smt. Sarla Verma case '15' multiplier is applicable in present case.
ii) The PW.1 in her chief examination deposed that her husband was working as mason and earning Rs.18,000/- per month.
In order to prove the income of deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents that he was earning a sum of Rs.18,000/- p.m.
In the absence of positive documents regarding his occupation and income this Tribunal will consider notional income.
The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, fixed notional income of the year 2020 at 14,500/-p.m.
For determination of income before Lok- adalath for the Districts coming under the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Principal Benches, Bengaluru.

So in view of fixing of notional income by the Hon'ble High Court of Vasanthi vs Channakeshava on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92912475/
11 Karnataka, it is just and proper to this Tribunal to follow the notional income as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of  SCCH-9 15 MVC.No.1763/2020 Karnataka to decide the cases before this Tribunal also.

sentences.text: The petitioners have not produced any relevant document to prove the income of deceased.
Accordingly, the notional income of deceased during the year 2020 treated as Rs.14,500/- p.m., as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.
iii) With regard to the loss of future prospectus is concerned,
the Hon'ble Apex court in the decision reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 SC ( National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others.) held as under:-

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 SC ( National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "In case the deceased was self employed  or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40% of  the established income should be the  warrant where the deceased was below the  age of 40 year.

An addition of 25% where  the deceased was between the age of 40 to  50 years and 10% where the deceased was  between the age of 50 to 60 years, should  be regarded as the necessary method of  computation.
The established income  means the income minus the tax  component"
In the case on hand, deceased was aged about 40 years.

Hence, in view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, petitioners are entitled for additional 25%
 SCCH-9 16 MVC.No.1763/2020 of salary to the future prospectus.

So, the total gross Vasanthi vs Channakeshava on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92912475/
12 income of deceased would Rs.18,125/-p.m (Rs.14,500 +
Rs.3625/-)

Admittedly deceased Srinivasa was married,
petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 & 3 are the daughters considered as a legal heirs and dependents of the deceased.
So, petitioners are depending upon the income of deceased.

So, as per dictum of Hon'ble Supreme court in Smt.Sarla Verma case, where number of dependent family members is 2 to 3, 1/3rd has to be deducted from the gross income of deceased towards his personal expenses and remaining is to be taken as dependency.

Therefore, after deducting 1/3rd from gross income it would comes at Rs.12,083/-= (18,125 - 6,042).
v) Thus petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.21,74,940/-=(12,083x12xM15) as loss of dependency.
(B) Towards Consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses;

In view of Judgment of Hon'ble  SCCH-9 17 MVC.No.1763/2020 Supreme court of India, in between United India Insurance Co. Ltd V/s Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and others in Civil Appeal No.2705 of 2020 &
National insurance company LTD V/s Pranay Sethi and Ors, the petitioner No.1 being the wife, petitioner No.2 & 3 being the daughters of deceased are entitled Vasanthi vs Channakeshava on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92912475/
13 Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of spousal and Filial Consortium and they are also entitled for Rs.15,000/-
towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses.
 16.

Thus, the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads as under:
 Sl. Particulars Amount  No.
 a. Towards loss of dependency Rs.21,74,940/-
 and loss of future income  b. Towards Consortium  1. Spousal Consortium Rs.40,000/-
 2. Filial Consortium Rs.80,000/-

c. Towards Loss of Estate Rs.15,000/-
 d. Towards Funeral Expenses Rs.15,000/-
17. Regarding Liability:
The 2nd respondent has contended that policy issued in favour of respondent No.1 is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
On perusal of entire materials there is no material is available to show the respondent No.1, who is the owner of offending vehicle has violated the conditions of the policy.
Even the 2nd respondent has not established 1st respondent has violated terms and condition of the policy.
Under such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer are liable to pay the compensation.
As already stated above, the accident in question was caused by the driver of offending vehicle.
The Vasanthi vs Channakeshava on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92912475/
14 petitioners have proved that the accident was caused by the driver of the offending vehicle.
Under such circumstances, the respondent No.1 and 2 are liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

However, the respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle is primarily liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.

Accordingly,
I answer Issue No.3 answered Partly in the  SCCH-9 19 MVC.No.1763/2020 Affirmative.
 18.
Issue No.4:

For the aforesaid reasons and discussion, the tribunal proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.23,24,940/- (Rupees Twenty Three Lakhs Twenty Four Thousand Nine Hundred Forty Only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.

The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners and respondent No.2 being insurer primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.

The apportionment of compensation to the petitioners is as under:
petitioner No.1 = 60% petitioner No.2 = 20% petitioner No.3 = 20%

In total amount apportioned to the share of petitioner No.1 & 3, 60% of the amount shall be released in their favour and remaining 40% of the amount shall be deposited in their names in Karnataka Bank City Civil Court Branch, Bengaluru for a period of 3 years without encumbrance.

In total amount apportioned to the share of petitioner No.2 an entire amount shall be deposited in her name in the above bank till she attains the age of majority or for a Vasanthi vs Channakeshava on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92912475/
15 period of three years whichever is later.
However the periodical interest may be drawn by the petitioner No.1 who is next friend of petitioner No.2 for her educational expenses.
The advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
